paper: A hyperbolic-regularized Casson model for pulsatile blood flow simulation in a rigid artery
what_it_does: Jeffreys viscoelastic model for shear stress + Casson regularised by PAPANASTASIOU (1987) for apparent viscosity
1-D pulsatile flow in a rigid tube, solved in Mathematica and FORTRAN
studies the effect of dimensionless yield stress Y0, relaxation time tauR0, retardation time tauR1
reports that the PHYSICAL plug radius grows with Y0, reducing mean velocity and raising friction factor
mesh convergence: a single sentence, '200 intervals obtained convergence in three significant digits'
what_it_does_NOT_do: different regularisation FAMILY: Papanastasiou exponential stress growth, not a bi-viscosity / nuMax ceiling
no study of the regularisation parameter's effect on the COMPUTED plug width
no cost or mesh-resolution scaling with the regularisation parameter
no measurability coupling (the mesh needed to resolve the defect scaling with the cap)
the plug discussion is about the PHYSICAL yield-stress effect, not the regularisation artefact
outcome: NARROWS finding 1 but does not close it. Regularised Casson in haemodynamics is established, so no novelty there. The specific contribution that survives is the measurability/cost coupling - that resolving a cap defect of relative size eps needs N > 1/(xi*sqrt(nu_c/nuMax)) while convergence cost grows as ~N^2*nuMax, so the two requirements forbid the same corner. Not present here, and not in Frigaard & Nouar's error-order framing either.
